pr_title: security:	cache certificate expiration metrics as pointers
pr_body:
security:	cache certificate expiration metrics as pointers

Changes in #130110 were added to add labelled ttl metrics to client certificates. It achieved this by changing the system which cached certificate expiries to cache on a composite struct of two metrics, rather than just an expiration metric.

The struct itself housed the metrics as inline values, rather than pointers, so updates were registered in the cached values only, and not the registry in which they were reporting. This means that updates to client certificate expirations would not be reflected by the ttl or expiration metrics.

This ticket modifies those elements so that they are not copied when they are pulled from the cache.

Fixes: #142681
Epic: CRDB-40209

Release note (bug fix): Fixes bug in client certificate expiration metrics.

issue_context.title: security: updating client certificates does not update the corresponding child metric
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**
Changes in #130110 were added to add labelled ttl metrics to client certificates. It achieved this by changing the system which cached certificate expiries to cache on a composite struct of two metrics, rather than just an expiration metric.

The struct itself housed the metrics as inline values, rather than pointers, so updates were registered in the cached values only, and not the registry in which they were reporting. This means that updates to client certificate expirations would not be reflected by the ttl or expiration metrics.

**To Reproduce**

First start the server:
```
./cockroach cert create-ca --certs-dir=./certs --ca-key=./certs/ca.key
./cockroach cert create-node localhost 127.0.0.1 --certs-dir=certs --ca-key=certs/ca.key --lifetime=8759
./cockroach start-single-node --certs-dir=./certs
```

Then create a root certificate which expires in 100 hours (roughly 360000 seconds):
```
./cockroach cert create-client root --certs-dir=./certs --ca-key=./certs/ca.key --lifetime '100h0m0s'
./cockroach sql --certs-dir=./certs --user=root
```

Verify the expiry is near the target of 360000:
```
$ curl -k https://localhost:8080/_status/vars | grep security_certificate_ttl_client | grep root
security_certificate_ttl_client{node_id="1",sql_user="root"} 359984
```

Now change the certificate so that it expires in 1 hour:
```
./cockroach cert create-client root --certs-dir=./certs --ca-key=./certs/ca.key --lifetime '1h0m0s'
./cockroach sql --certs-dir=./certs --user=root
```

Verify the expiry hasn't changed on the cert metric:
```
security_certificate_ttl_client{node_id="1",sql_user="root"} 359900
```


**Expected behavior**

**Additional data / screenshots**
Original discussion thread: https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C063CP41TG9/p1741372454363459

**Environment:**
 - CockroachDB version [e.g. 24.1.0+]

**Additional context**
Teams wishing to report or alert on near-expiration certificates by app will be operating on inaccurate information.


Epic CRDB-40209
